title: MD-102: Microsoft 365 Endpoint Administrator
description: Prepares for Microsoft's exam MD-102 (Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate): Microsoft Entra ID for devices, Intune enrolment, compliance and Conditional Access, Windows Autopilot and provisioning, configuration profiles, Windows updates, monitoring and remote actions, apps and app protection, and endpoint security with BitLocker and LAPS. Practised in a pretend admin portal with simulated Windows PCs and phones.
disclaimer: Cert Lab is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Microsoft. Microsoft, Windows, Intune, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft 365, Defender and Autopilot are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. This course follows Microsoft's public "skills measured" outline for exam MD-102 as Cert Lab understood it in 2026 (four areas: Prepare infrastructure for devices, about 25-30%; Manage and maintain devices, about 30-35%; Manage applications, about 15-20%; Protect devices, about 15-20%). The weights are approximate and Microsoft changes the outline from time to time: check the current study guide on Microsoft Learn before you book the exam. Every lesson, question and lab was written for Cert Lab; none comes from Microsoft's exams or training. The admin portal and the devices are a simulation written by Cert Lab: they behave like Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Entra ID for what the course covers, but nothing signs in anywhere and nothing reaches a real service or this PC.
examNote: A Cert Lab practice exam in the style of Microsoft's: single and multiple answer questions, drag-and-order questions, Yes / No statement series, a case study (a scenario with several questions), and a few hands-on tasks in the practice portal. Scores are shown from 1 to 1000 with 700 to pass, like Microsoft's reports; Microsoft doesn't publish how its scores are calculated, so this is only an approximation (each item's points as a share of the total). Results are shown per objective, and the review explains every answer. Some names and numbers change from one attempt to the next.
examHint: Hands-on tasks are done in the practice portal on the right (and on the pretend devices when a task says so). Policies reach a device at its next check-in: use Sync on the device, or Skip time. Questions: pick the answer or answers asked for; for a drag-and-order question, move the right actions into the answer list in the right order. Points are shown with each item.
aboutMachines:
The practice tenant belongs to Riverbend Outfitters (riverbend.example), a made-up outdoor clothing company. You are Alex Morgan (alex@riverbend.example), an Intune Administrator. The people are Jordan Lee and Priya Shah (Sales), Sam Ortiz (Finance), Nils Fischer (Warehouse), Ava Brooks (HR), Chen Wei (IT help desk) and an emergency access account. The devices are Windows laptops RB-LT-001 and RB-LT-002, a new laptop still in its out-of-box experience (RB-LT-003), a hybrid joined desktop (RB-DT-010) and an older desktop that can't run Windows 11 (RB-DT-007), a kiosk (RB-KIOSK-01), Sam's personal PC at home (SAM-HOME-PC, Entra registered), Jordan's iPhone and Priya's Android phone. The makers and models (Lumen Devices) are made up.

The portal is Cert Lab's own drawing, not Microsoft's: its blades follow the Intune admin center and Microsoft Entra admin center closely enough to practise the clicks, with shorter labels in places. Devices check in about every 8 hours; Sync makes a device check in now, and Skip time moves the clock (monthly updates come out on the second Tuesday). Each Windows device has the simulated PowerShell console (dsregcmd /status, Get-BitLockerVolume, Get-MpComputerStatus...) and a pretend Settings > Accounts > Access work or school page.
